title: Northforge - Dedicated Reserve Qualification and Surge Strategy
summary: Discovery call to qualify Northforge's need for reserved GPU capacity. Covered isolation requirements, warm-pool prewarm strategy, eviction tolerances, fallback to hosted variants, compliance (KMS/SOC2), and next steps to run a surge simulation and share pricing + security pack.
topics: onprem vs VPC private control plane
action_items: Maya - Send dedicated pricing tiers, prewarm cost model spreadsheet - due 2026-11-30
Ravi - Share sample surge-sim script and benchmark checklist - due 2026-12-02
Priya - Provide expected peak qps and sequence length distribution (CSV) - due 2026-11-29
Tanya - Request SOC2 + network architecture whitepaper from Redwood - due 2026-11-30
next_steps: Redwood to run surge-sim using Northforge traces
Customer to confirm required isolation level (node vs GPU slice)
Schedule a 60m deep-dive with infra + security (SE-led) next week
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-25 15:00 PST, Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ravi (Redwood SE), Lena (Redwood Solutions), Jordan (Redwood CS), Ethan (Northforge HoML), Priya (Platform Eng), Sam (SRE), Tanya (Security), Lee (Product)

00:00 - Maya: ok hey everyone thanks for carving out time, um quick intros on our side, i'm maya ae, ravi is our se who focuses on dedicated runtime and prewarm strategies.
00:12 - Ethan: yeah hi thanks, i'm ethan, head of ml at northforge, we run a mix of retrieval+generation workloads, mostly inference for chat assistants and some batch embeddings.
00:22 - Priya: hey i'm priya, platform, we're owning infra side and want to understand isolation and eviction behavior.
00:30 - Maya: great, high level we wanted to qualify if dedicated reserved capacity makes sense vs hosted, and dig into burst patterns, prewarm cost tradeoffs, and security needs.
01:05 - Ravi: quick question up front, are you expecting hard single-digit ms latency for interactive queries or is 50-150ms acceptable? that's going to drive hot vs warm pool sizing and prewarm cadence.
01:22 - Ethan: interactive is important, aiming for median 120ms tail 95 under 300ms ideally. Cost matters too, we have spikes during business hours and big nightly batch runs.
01:40 - Sam: also we want isolation; we can't have noisy neighbor interference. What's your node tenancy approach?
01:50 - Ravi: we offer dedicated pools where you reserve whole nodes or fractional provisioning depending on model. for strict isolation you can reserve tenant-isolated nodes (single-customer). less strict, we can multi-tenant with tenant fencing: cgroups + GPU MIG for supported hw. there's also an intermediate hotpool approach where prewarmed containers are sticky to your account.
02:20 - Priya: sticky is interesting. how does eviction work if a node is reclaimed for cluster balancing?
02:30 - Ravi: we have eviction windows and preemptive drain hooks. reserved capacity means you get priority and eviction tolerance is configurable. we can set SLA-backed compute weights; eviction usually only in extreme cloud-level incidents. for private/onprem we do not evict unless customer opts in.
03:00 - Tanya: security question: KMS integration for model keys and customer data, and SOC2 attestations?
03:08 - Lena: yes, we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations in private deployments; hosted offers KMS with envelope encryption and audit logs. we are SOC2 Type II certified and can share the report under NDA.
03:28 - Ethan: Cool, you mentioned fallback to hosted variants, can we failover gracefully if our reserved pool hits capacity during a flash?
03:36 - Ravi: yes we support smart routing and fallback policies — you can set a policy to route overflow to a compatible hosted model variant (quantized or lower-capacity model) with throttles. there's also burst capacity buys for short durations.
04:10 - Maya: can you walk through a typical burst scenario? maybe show how prewarm, kv cache and batching interact?
04:20 - Ravi: sure. imagine a sudden 5x qps spike. the runtime tries to respond from KV cache for repeated prefixes. if not available, we pull from warm pool VMs that have cached model weights and kv caches warm. we also employ continuous batching within short windows to improve throughput. if warm pool exhausted, we either spin up burst nodes (if you have purchased burst credits) or overflow to hosted lane.
05:05 - Sam: how long to spin up burst nodes — minutes?
05:10 - Ravi: depends on region and instance type — typically 2-6 minutes for a cold spin, but our hotpool can reduce that to seconds for a limited number of prewarmed slots. the tradeoff is cost for idle prewarmed capacity.
05:30 - Priya: what's the accounting model for prewarm vs reserved? do we pay full node price for a hotpool slot?
05:38 - Maya: reserved capacity billed as monthly commit; hotpool prewarm is an add-on priced hourly for prewarmed slots. we provide a cost model spreadsheet that simulates different prewarm sizes against your traffic profile.
06:05 - Ethan: can we mix on-prem for sensitive models and hosted for public ones?
06:12 - Lena: yes, hybrid is common — private control plane with on-prem nodes for regulated models and hosted/dedicated in cloud for lower-sensitivity workloads. routing policies handle model variants and data tagging.
06:30 - Priya: curious about per-tenant quotas inside the reserved pool — we want to squash runaway jobs.
06:38 - Ravi: we have per-tenant quota enforcement and circuit breakers. you can set QPS caps, token-rate limits, and concurrent job caps. plus tracing so you can see token-level cost.
07:00 - Lee: any constraints on sequence length or context windows that change kernel selection?
07:08 - Ravi: yes longer context changes memory; runtime picks kernels and may use KV spilling strategies. we recommend profiling with real sequences; our optimizer suggests quantization or padding strategies to reduce mem.
07:40 - Ethan: ok can you run a surge sim with our traces? we'd like to see projected tail latency and cost.
07:45 - Maya: absolutely — ravi will run a surge sim; we just need a sample trace or distribution and some env constraints.
07:55 - Priya: we'll provide a CSV with qps per minute, median seq len, percentiles.
08:05 - Ravi: perfect, with that we'll model three configs: conservative reserved nodes (isolated), smaller reserve + hotpool, and reserve + fallback to hosted. we'll show cost and latency tradeoffs.
08:30 - Ethan: what about pre-warming sticky to sessions — e.g., we have burst to a subset of users and want low jitter for those sessions?
08:40 - Ravi: session affinity in our hotpool is achievable by pinning a warm slot to a customer session cookie; it's limited by warm pool size. otherwise, continuous KV caching helps repeated prompts.
09:00 - Sam: recovery scenarios — if a reserved node fails mid-batch, what's the failover path?
09:07 - Ravi: requests in flight are retried; KV cache cold miss may add latency, we have graceful degradation with shorter responses or rate-limiting with error codes so upstream can fallback. plus we support canary traffic mirroring for rollouts.
09:40 - Tanya: from compliance standpoint, we need audit logs for model access and key rotations. is that available?
09:48 - Lena: yes audit logs, key rotation logs, and per-token metadata retention policies. for private deployments you can ship logs to your SIEM.
10:10 - Ethan: curious about eviction tolerance numbers — like how many minutes of warm state we lose on graceful preemption?
10:18 - Ravi: warm state depends on what you're caching. weights are persisted; KV cache can be checkpointed occasionally but ephemeral. for hotpool slots, eviction usually means losing KV caches and needing 10-90s to rebuild depending on usage; full cold spin is minutes. we'll provide more exact numbers after we see the trace patterns.
11:00 - Maya: can we talk about security posture for hybrid — if we run private control plane with cloud-hosted inference, how are network flows and customer keys handled?
11:10 - Lena: private control plane keeps control-plane metadata in your VPC, runtime nodes can run in your account and we integrate via peering or private links. keys live in your KMS; Redwood holds zero plaintext keys.
11:30 - Priya: any blockers for our onprem evaluation — we have air-gapped env for PHI models.
11:36 - Lena: for air-gap we have an on-prem package, installation runbook, and a support SLA. some features that require cloud telemetry are limited; we can list them.
12:05 - Sam: ok cost question again — if we overprovision reserve for headroom we pay idle costs, what's the typical approach?
12:14 - Maya: Many customers start with a smaller reserved footprint + hotpool and measure; then expand to full reserved when predictability matters. reserved is best when steady baseline traffic exists; hotpool handles spikes.
12:32 - Ethan: what about eviction policies if the infra team needs to reclaim nodes for infra ops, we'd need explicit quarantine windows.
12:39 - Ravi: we offer maintenance windows and soft preemption notifications with drain period. you can set the minimum drain to ensure in-flight completes or redirect.
13:00 - Priya: we need to surface per-route cost for product owners. is that in the console?
13:05 - Jordan: yes console has per-route token breakdown, cost, latency histograms, and model versioning. you can annotate routes to teams.
13:25 - Ethan: any compatibility issues with custom kernels or model ops? we use some custom ops in our tokenizer pipeline.
13:32 - Ravi: we support custom ops at build time for private/onprem. hosted has restrictions; SEs can help with a compatibility assessment.
14:00 - Maya: ok i want to capture success criteria — ethan, what would success look like for Northforge after a pilot?
14:08 - Ethan: pilot demonstrates median latency under 150ms for 99% of steady traffic, ability to absorb 2x production spikes with acceptable tail under 500ms, and a cost model that is within our runway — plus SOC2 docs for final approvals.
14:30 - Maya: perfect. we'll map deliverables to that.
15:00 - Priya: timeline — we aim for pilot in jan, procurement signed by end of q1.
15:07 - Maya: noted.
15:15 - Ravi: technical note — if you're sensitive to model drift, we can pin model revisions per route and do A/B rollouts with automatic fallback.
15:28 - Ethan: good, we do A/B often.
15:35 - Tanya: one more on keys — rotation cadence and removal on offboarding?
15:40 - Lena: we roll with customer KMS; rotation is controlled by you. revoking access triggers immediate removal of runtime access; logs show last access times.
16:00 - Sam: are there constraints on heterogeneous GPU fleets? we may have some A100 and some L4.
16:08 - Ravi: runtime can route jobs to hardware classes based on SLOs; model compilation chooses kernels per gpu class. mixing is fine but you need to model perf differences; we'll include that in the sim.
16:30 - Ethan: ok what's the path to get pricing for a 24/7 reserve vs hybrid?
16:36 - Maya: i'll send tiered pricing and an example spreadsheet — that's on the action items.
16:48 - Priya: what about billing for burst — do we get a fixed burst bucket or pay per minute?
16:54 - Maya: both options exist: burst credits bought as a block (cheaper) or pay-as-you-go for variable usage. we'll include both scenarios.
17:10 - Ethan: i'm worried about cold-start variance during peak — can we simulate worst-case 99.9th percentile?
17:18 - Ravi: yes surge-sim will produce P50/P95/P99/P999 with and without KV cache; we'll show sensitivity to warm pool size.
17:45 - Lee: can we have a brief sketch of rollout plan if we choose Redwood Dedicated?
17:50 - Jordan: typical flow: pilot (2-4 weeks) using reserved small footprint + hotpool; validate perf; then expand reserve and set up SSO/SAML, KMS integration, and run a compliance review. we provide runbooks for oncall and alerting.
18:20 - Priya: alerting — do you emit infra and application-level alerts into our pager?
18:26 - Jordan: yes we integrate with PagerDuty/Slack/Datadog. token-level cost anomalies and tail latency alerts are supported.
18:50 - Ethan: what about data residency? some models run only in eu-west.
18:55 - Lena: we can pin regions for model hosting and provide regional control planes for private deployments.
19:10 - Tanya: ok we'll need the security pack ASAP.
19:15 - Maya: we'll attach the security pack and SOC2 under NDA.
19:28 - Ethan: anything else on scaling expectations?
19:32 - Ravi: final note - autoscaling is config-driven: scale by token-rate or GPU utilization; we recommend token-rate for better lambda with sequence variance.
19:50 - Priya: good.
20:00 - Maya: Recap: Redwood to run surge-sim (Ravi), send pricing/spreadsheet (Maya), share security pack (Lena). Northforge to send traces and seq distribution (Priya) and confirm isolation level (Ethan).
20:20 - Ethan: yes we'll provide those by end of week.
20:30 - Maya: schedule follow-up se deep-dive for next tuesday?
20:36 - Priya:Tuesday works.
20:40 - Maya: great, thank you all.
20:45 - (meeting ends)

Notes about transcript: occasional mis-heard words, e.g., "hotpool" transcribed sometimes as "hot pool" or "hot-pull"; some speaker labels are slightly generic. The call included a live whiteboard share (referred to as "surge sim spreadsheet").
